Bus.question: Which work orders and incidents concern bus 4127?
Bus.why: Every maintenance question ends at a bus. It has an identity (its fleet number), a history of work and incidents, and is referred to across the policy, the incident review and the work orders.
Bus.alternatives: Considered keeping the bus as a text field on the work order; rejected because the incident review and the work orders must point at the same bus to be compared.

Garage.question: Which work orders are open at East Garage, and what stock does it hold?
Garage.why: Work, stock and PM permissions are all per garage, and the Bus 4127 incident turned on East Garage lacking a part Central Garage had.
Garage.alternatives: A plain location string; rejected because PM levels, stock and work orders all need to point at the same garage.

WorkOrder.question: Which work orders are open at a garage, and which parts did WO-2291 use?
WorkOrder.why: The work order is the unit the Maintenance Supervisor assigns and closes; it has its own number, dates and state, and links a bus, a garage, parts and sometimes an incident.
WorkOrder.alternatives: Folding repairs into the incident report; rejected because PM work orders have no incident, and one incident can lead to several work orders.

IncidentReport.question: Which incidents involved bus 4127, and which work orders came from them?
IncidentReport.why: The policy requires the Safety Officer to review every incident report, and a work order raised after an incident must cite it: the report is what both point at.
IncidentReport.alternatives: Modelling the incident (the event) and its report separately; deferred: no question yet distinguishes when it happened from when it was written beyond the occurred_on date.

PMLevel.question: What is the PM-B interval, and which garages may perform it?
PMLevel.why: Intervals and permitted garages change over time (PM-B moved to 20,000 km and to East Garage in September 2025), so each level must be a node whose facts can be superseded with dates.
PMLevel.alternatives: A status field on each bus saying which PM is due; rejected because a status keeps no history and no reason for a change.

Part.question: Which parts did a work order use?
Part.why: The Bus 4127 review turned on one part number (BRK-221): which work orders used it and where it was stocked. A part has an identity shared by work orders and stock counts.
Part.alternatives: Part numbers as free text on the work order; rejected because the stock count and the work order must name the same part to be joined.

StockLevel.question: How many BRK-221 does East Garage hold, and when must it reorder?
StockLevel.why: Stock is a fact about a part AT a garage, counted on a date. Putting quantities on Part would merge two things: the same part has different counts and reorder points at each garage.
StockLevel.alternatives: Quantities as attributes of Part; rejected by the 'one thing or two merged' test. Quantities on a stocked_at edge; rejected because the count needs its own date and source to be superseded each quarter.

Role.question: Who must review an incident report, and who approves a change to a PM level?
Role.why: The policy assigns duties to positions (Fleet Manager, Safety Officer, Maintenance Supervisor), not to named people. People move; the role and its duties stay.
Role.alternatives: A Person class for Dana Reyes and others; rejected for now: no question needs an individual's decisions traced. The person who said something is recorded on the captured source instead.

Route.question: Which buses run route 12, and which work orders touched them?
Route.why: Dana wants incidents and repairs grouped by route: a route with hills wears brakes faster, and Bus 4127 failed on Route 12.
Route.alternatives: Route as a text attribute on Bus; rejected because buses change routes and the assignment needs its own dates.

raised_at.question: Which work orders are open at East Garage?
raised_at.why: This is where the work is carried out, which is not always the bus's home garage: Bus 4127 was repaired at East Garage with parts from Central Garage.

stocks.question: Which parts does East Garage stock, and does WO-2291 use one it does not?
stocks.why: The Bus 4127 delay came from a work order needing a part its garage had no stock of. The stock sheet only states counts, so the garage-to-part link is derived from them rather than authored twice.
